topic: Spark Center panel fixes the DGX Spark's stock updates
title: DGX Spark updates fixed by Spark Center
description: The DGX Spark's stock Dashboard updates every apt package it can find, then forces a reboot. Spark Center, an MIT-licensed open-source panel from one maintainer, lets you pick packages, simulates the dependency changes first, samples the GPU every two seconds, and flags firmware flashes that claim success without changing the version; its own README warns that ticking the kernel without NVIDIA's signed modules costs you the GPU driver. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: One button updates everything on the DGX Spark.
You press Update. The Spark decides.
Your Spark just updated Chrome. By itself.
One button, no brakes, one forced reboot.
The Spark's update button has no brakes.
A 128 GB AI box, updating Chrome on its own.
Your Spark reboots mid-update. On purpose.
One maintainer just fixed NVIDIA's update button.
128 GB of memory, zero update choices.
The DGX Spark updates what it wants.
narration_full: You press Update, and the Spark decides. One hundred twenty-eight gigabytes of memory. It upgrades Chrome. That button drives apt, the package installer, across every repository. Then it reboots. Now the Spark gets brakes. Spark Center, one owner's open-source panel. You pick packages. A simulation shows what it will touch. It never reboots. The monitor samples the GPU every two seconds. It catches the chip stuck at six hundred eleven megahertz. A firmware flash can claim success and change nothing. Spark Center reads fwupd, the Linux firmware tool, and flags it. The catch: the kernel without NVIDIA's signed modules means no GPU driver. The DGX Dashboard decided everything. Now you decide.
